tasks.title: Freeze the deployable custom branch and create the isolated worktree
tasks.detail:
Goal: guarantee the deployable checkout can never be damaged by the rebase work, and give the rebase its own working tree.
Files: no repo files. Git metadata only: tag `fork-deploy-0.9.3`, worktree /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream, branch `custom-next`.
Contract: main checkout /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web stays on branch `custom` at commit 7092dba with a clean `git status`; the live `pm2 pi-web-custom` app (port 4201, next-server) must keep running because it hosts the active agent session.
Steps:
1. cd /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web; confirm `git status --porcelain` prints nothing.
2. `git tag -f fork-deploy-0.9.3 custom` so the pre-rebase deploy point is named.
3. `git worktree add -b custom-next /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream custom`.
4. Never run npm install, npm run build, or git checkout in the main checkout afterwards.
Verify: `git -C /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web status -sb` shows `## custom...origin/custom` and no changes; `git -C /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints `custom-next`; `lsof -nP -iTCP:4201 -sTCP:LISTEN` still lists the next-server process.
Done when: the tag exists, the worktree is on custom-next at 7092dba, and the running app is untouched.

tasks.title: Install the worktree and record a green 0.9.3 baseline
tasks.detail:
Goal: prove the worktree reproduces the current fork behaviour before any rebase, so later failures are attributable to the rebase.
Files: writes only to worktree-local node_modules/ (untracked). Must not touch the main checkout.
Contract: run everything with cwd /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream.
Steps:
1. `npm install` (installs pi SDK 0.87.1 from the committed lockfile; postinstall runs bin/prepare-terminal.js).
2. `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` — record the exit code and the first failures, if any.
3. `npm test` — record pass/fail counts.
4. Append the three results to this task's progress field via `ppm`.
Verify: tsc exits 0 and `npm test` reports no failing test. Any pre-existing failure is recorded as a baseline defect, not fixed here.
Done when: baseline typecheck and unit tests are recorded as evidence.
